values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/reedgreenbridge ('There are seven sites for tent and small trailer use'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (7 campsites), read 2026-10-25

summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: $20, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only, 15-day max (were inherited or absent, now stated for this campground), 7 sites (derived -> manual). 'Tent and small trailer' boilerplate agrees with the --AWH 'Small campers only'; note kept verbatim. Season left (manual; see flag). Type 'rustic', not equestrian; ORVs 'allowed in the campground to enter and exit only' via a parallel county road to Luce County ORV routes, not an ORV trail camp. Access 29 mi N of Newberry via M-123 and County Roads 500, 407 and 410; no road warning on the page.
flags: Phone missing: the DNR campground page and the amenity table give 906-492-3415 (Tahquamenon Falls State Park, the managing park).
Name: the DNR page and the amenity table call it 'Reed & Green Bridge State Forest Campground'; the entry has 'Reed & Green Campground'.

Season conflict between two DNR pages: the amenity table gives 'Seasonal closure dates: Nov. 30 – May 1' (the stored manual season, May 1 - Nov 29), but the campground page says 'This rustic campground is open all year; however, the campground and seasonal roads are not plowed.' Stored season left as is.
